title: Representative Ciscomani highlights $1 million for Cochise County law enforcement communications
text:
Representative Ciscomani highlights $1 million for Cochise County law enforcement communications
J. E. Carter
Representative Juan Ciscomani visited the Cochise County Sheriff’s Office in Sierra Vista, AZ on Aug. 26 to highlight $1 million in federal funding preliminarily secured to enhance the department’s communications capabilities and provide local law enforcement with additional tools.
The funding is intended for the purchase of four mobile communications trailers that will deliver 5G data and P25-compliant radio coverage for the Cochise County Sheriff’s Department. These trailers are designed to be moved throughout the county, which spans over 6,000 square miles and is home to nearly 126,000 residents. The investment aims to help deputies maintain reliable communication without building permanent infrastructure and is expected to save about $140,000 annually in communications costs.
"I am incredibly proud to be fighting to deliver $1 million to the Cochise County Sheriff’s Department," said Representative Ciscomani. "Our local law enforcement officers deserve the tools and resources necessary to carry out their mission and keep our communities safe. This targeted investment will improve communications for drone operations, search-and-rescue command and control, and high-definition video surveillance, helping our officers better serve the people of Cochise County. I will always fight for our local heroes, and I am confident this meaningful investment will have a lasting impact on Cochise County residents, visitors, and businesses for years to come."
Cochise County Sheriff Mark Dannels also commented on Ciscomani's involvement: "Our office and our entire community is grateful for Representative Ciscomani’s leadership and partnership in working to deliver this $1 million to Cochise County. We saw the need to improve our communications systems, and when we brought that need to Congressman Ciscomani, he didn’t hesitate to make it a priority. We appreciate his efforts to make this investment a reality for our local law enforcement and the people we serve," said Dannels.
Before visiting the department, Representative Ciscomani attended an ATF K-9 demonstration recognizing National Dog Day that showcased how K-9 teams assist both federal and local law enforcement across Arizona.
Ciscomani serves as Arizona's only congressional delegation member on the House Appropriations Committee. The $1 million allocation is part of $42.7 million preliminarily secured through Community Project Funding requests across Arizona's 6th Congressional District; previously he secured $60 million between Fiscal Years 2024–2026 through similar projects, according to Representative Juan Ciscomani's office. He has represented Arizona’s 6th district since replacing Ann Kirkpatrick in 2023.
